sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vivek Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- Ashutosh Pandey,G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.
2. List has been revised.

3. Heard Sri Vivek Singh learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Akash Kumar Sharma, Advocate holding brief of Sri Ashutosh Pandey, learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 368 of 2024 under Sections 323, 354, 376, 506 I.P.C.
Police Station Hathras Gate, District Hathras during the pendency of trial.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The F.I.R. was instituted with the allegations that applicant had outraged the modesty of victim.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The allegation of outraging the modesty of victim have been escalated to that of rape at the stage of recording of her statement under Section 183 B.N.S.S.
The said allegations have been made after legal consultation.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that there is no medical corroboration of the incident.
Criminal history of three cases assigned to the applicant have been explained.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 25.07.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
8.
Learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the bail application.

9. The Supreme Court in Jaya Mala vs. State of J & K, (1982) 2 SCC 538 and Mohd. Imran Khan vs.
State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), (2011) 10 SCC 192

sentences.text: has opined that the radiologist cannot predict the correct date of birth rather there is a long margin of 1 to 2 years on either side.

10. The Supreme Court in the case of Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785 has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Rahul Chaudhary, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in Rahul Chaudhary vs State Of U.P. on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47498548/

entities.text: Rahul Chaudhary vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 accordance with law.

13. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
14.

It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
